data.name: Marimuthu
data.gender_notes: Marimuthu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Marimuthu is derived from the Sanskrit words 'mari' which means 'sea' and 'muthu' which means 'love'. This name is associated with the divine ocean of love and devotion. In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is often referred to as 'Mari Muthu' and is believed to bestow his blessings upon those who invoke him with this name. The name Marimuthu carries the meaning “Sea of Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Marimuthu usually hope their child will grow to embody sea of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Marimuthu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sea of Love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marimuthu total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Marimuthu was a famous Chola warrior and commander during the reign of Rajaraja Chola I (985-1014 CE). He is best known for his victory over the Pandyas at the Battle of Sullurupeta in 1003 CE.

Marimuthu II was a powerful Nayak ruler in the late 16th and early 17th centuries. He ruled over the provinces of Nattankottai and Tirukkoyilur, and is known for establishing a strong military presence and expanding his territory.
